articles.title: Despite El Nino, initial figures on soybean production in MP are encouraging: CM Mohan Yadav
articles.description: Indore, Oct 16 (PTI): Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav said on Friday that despite the reduction in monsoon rainfall this year due to the impact of El Nino, initial figures on soybean production in the state are encouraging. He said that Madhya Pradesh is among the major soybean-producing states in the country and the state government is promoting agriculture-based industries and processing activities. Addressing the International Soybean Conference in Indore, the chief minister said, "The impact of El Niño this year was beyond anyone's control, but by God's grace, sometimes disasters in Madhya Pradesh bring opportunities. I am happy that the current figures on soybean production in the state are encouraging." He said that Madhya Pradesh is also seen as the country's "food basket" and the state accounts for about 45 per cent of the national soybean acreage. The state government is celebrating 2026 as the "Year of Farmer Welfare", and special attention is being paid to promoting agriculture and related sectors during this period, he said. Yadav informed that the cabinet recently approved a new industrial corridor connecting Jabalpur, Bhopal and Indore. Businessmen, scientists, and industry representatives from various countries are attending the International Soybean Conference, which began on Friday in Indore, the economic capital of Madhya Pradesh. The conference will last for two days. PTI HWP MAS SKY SKY (This story is published as part of the auto-generated syndicate wire feed. No editing has been done in the headline or the body by ABP Live.)

articles.title: No meddling as 'middlemen' in forex conversion by banks: New rules forbid conversion of foreign earnings into rupees to detriment of exporters
articles.description: The Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India (FEDAI) has directed banks not to convert foreign currency remittances into rupees without specific instructions from the sender or beneficiary. The move follows concerns that intermediary banks were converting dollars at unfavourable exchange rates, leaving small exporters and individuals receiving overseas payments with less money. Banks have also been asked to ensure transparent forex service charges and disclose currency conversion rates on their websites.
